nodes.summary: If a finite directed graph $G$, given by a vertex enumeration and adjacency lists, is acyclic, then deterministic FIFO Kahn topological sorting of $G$ returns success with some vertex order.
nodes.title: Kahn's algorithm succeeds on acyclic graphs

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph and let $R$ and $c = [c_1, \dots, c_k]$ be lists of vertices. Then $c$ is a directed cycle of $G$ in $R$ if and only if $k \ge 1$, the vertices $c_1, \dots, c_k$ are pairwise distinct, $G$ has an edge from $c_i$ to $c_{i+1}$ for every $1 \le i < k$, $G$ has an edge from $c_k$ to $c_1$, and every $c_i$ lies in $R$.
nodes.title: Characterization of directed cycles within a vertex list

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph and $R$ a list of vertices. A list $c = [c_1, \dots, c_k]$ of vertices is a directed cycle of $G$ in $R$ when $k \ge 1$, the vertices $c_1, \dots, c_k$ are pairwise distinct, $G$ has an edge from $c_i$ to $c_{i+1}$ for each $1 \le i < k$ and an edge from $c_k$ to $c_1$, and every $c_i$ lies in $R$.
nodes.title: Directed cycle within a vertex list

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph. If deterministic FIFO Kahn topological sorting of $G$ fails after processing the vertex list $P$ and leaving the vertex list $R$ unprocessed, then $G$ has a directed cycle in $R$: a nonempty list of pairwise distinct vertices of $R$ in which each vertex has an edge to the next and the last vertex has an edge to the first.
nodes.title: A failed Kahn run leaves a directed cycle

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph. If deterministic FIFO Kahn topological sorting of $G$ fails after processing the vertex list $P$ and leaving the vertex list $R$ unprocessed, then for every vertex $v$ in $R$ the indegree of $v$ within $R$, the number of entries $u$ of $R$ such that $G$ has an edge from $u$ to $v$, is positive.
nodes.title: Unprocessed vertices of a failed Kahn run have positive indegree among the unprocessed

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph. If deterministic FIFO Kahn topological sorting of $G$ fails after processing the vertex list $P$ and leaving the vertex list $R$ unprocessed, then $R$ is nonempty, neither $P$ nor $R$ has repeated entries, a vertex lies in the vertex list of $G$ if and only if it lies in $P$ or in $R$, and no vertex lies in both $P$ and $R$.
nodes.title: A failed Kahn run splits the vertices into processed and unprocessed ones

nodes.summary: For a finite directed graph $G$, a list $R$ of vertices and a vertex $v$, the indegree of $v$ within $R$ is the number of entries $u$ of $R$, counted with multiplicity, such that $G$ has an edge from $u$ to $v$.
nodes.title: Indegree within a vertex list

nodes.summary: The indegree of a vertex $v$ in a finite directed graph $G$ is the number of vertices $u$ such that $G$ has an edge from $u$ to $v$; repeated entries in adjacency lists count once.
nodes.title: Indegree

nodes.summary: A finite directed graph $G$ is acyclic if and only if there is no directed cycle of $G$ in its vertex list, that is, no nonempty list of pairwise distinct vertices in which each vertex has an edge to the next and the last vertex has an edge to the first.
nodes.title: Acyclicity means having no directed cycle

nodes.summary: A finite directed graph $G$ is acyclic when it has no directed cycle, that is, no nonempty list $[c_1, \dots, c_k]$ of pairwise distinct vertices such that $G$ has an edge from $c_i$ to $c_{i+1}$ for each $1 \le i < k$ and an edge from $c_k$ to $c_1$.
nodes.title: Acyclic directed graph

nodes.summary: A list $L$ of vertices of a finite directed graph $G$ is a topological order of $G$ when $L$ has no duplicates, a vertex lies in $L$ exactly when it lies in the vertex enumeration of $G$, and for every edge $u \to v$ of $G$ the first position of $u$ in $L$ is strictly smaller than the first position of $v$ in $L$.
nodes.title: Topological order

nodes.summary: The result of Kahn's topological sorting algorithm on a graph with vertices of type $\alpha$ is either a success, carrying a list of vertices, or a failure, carrying the list of vertices processed before the queue emptied and the list of vertices that remain.
nodes.title: Outcome of Kahn's topological sort

nodes.summary: Run Kahn's algorithm with a first-in first-out queue on a finite directed graph $G$ whose vertices are enumerated as $v_1, \dots, v_n$. Initially every vertex is remaining, the counter of each vertex is its number of in-neighbours, and the queue holds the vertices with no in-neighbours in enumeration order. At each of $n$ steps, if the queue is nonempty, its front vertex $x$ is removed from the queue and from the…
nodes.title: Kahn's topological sort

nodes.summary: For every finite directed graph $G$, Kahn's topological sort on $G$ returns a success if and only if $G$ is acyclic.
nodes.title: Kahn's algorithm succeeds exactly on acyclic graphs

nodes.summary: If Kahn's topological sort on a finite directed graph $G$ returns a success with list $L$, then a vertex lies in $L$ if and only if it lies in the vertex enumeration of $G$.
nodes.title: A successful topological sort lists every vertex

nodes.summary: If Kahn's topological sort on a finite directed graph $G$ returns a success with list $L$, then for every edge $u \to v$ of $G$ the first position of $u$ in $L$ is strictly smaller than the first position of $v$ in $L$.
nodes.title: A successful topological sort points every edge forward

nodes.summary: If Kahn's topological sort on a finite directed graph $G$ returns a success, then $G$ is acyclic.
nodes.title: Success of Kahn's algorithm implies acyclicity

nodes.summary: If Kahn's topological sort on a finite directed graph $G$ returns a success with list $L$, then $L$ is a topological order of $G$.
nodes.title: A successful topological sort is a topological order

nodes.summary: If Kahn's topological sort on a finite directed graph $G$ returns a success with list $L$, then $L$ has no duplicates.
nodes.title: A successful topological sort has no repeated vertex

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
